steps: Attacker obtains any authenticated session without tap_viewer/tap_admin.
Attacker discovers or guesses a panel URL id from a page/nav leak, seed data, or URL history.
If the panel is a ViewerPanel, attacker supplies entity_id and entity_type query parameters to render another object.
Sensitive page/panel/object fields are returned without grid.read and without authz-denial logging.

codeEvidence.explanation: The route reaches graph-backed Panel state and renders the panel template without calling authorize(..., "grid.read", ...).
codeEvidence.label: Panel view resolves and renders without authorization

codeEvidence.explanation: When used behind the unguarded panel endpoint, query parameters select an arbitrary registered entity type and entity id for direct ORM lookup.
codeEvidence.label: ViewerPanel resolves request-selected object

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace and live network validation agree: capless panel GET returned 200 while guarded object/API routes returned 403 and logged denials.

preventiveControls: Static route/ORM lint for graph model access in tap_web views and panel helpers unless preceded by an explicit authorize call.
Central helper for graph-read guarded panel/page resolution.
findings.remediation: Call tap_auth.policy.authorize(get_caller_context(), "grid.read", operation="panel_view") before any Panel lookup or panel-type context building. Add defense-in-depth grid.read authorization before ViewerPanel request-selected object resolution, and add no-cap HTTP tests proving panel fragments return 403 and emit authz-denial logs.
remediationTests: No-cap live HTTP GET /panel/<panel-url-id>/ returns 403 and emits [e5d9]/[a6b7].
No-cap live HTTP GET to a ViewerPanel with target entity query parameters returns 403.
tap_viewer can read panel fragments; tap_admin can read and edit where grid.write is required.

rootCause.summary: Panel fragments were treated as UI implementation details instead of graph-read entrypoints, so the route relies on downstream helpers that are not guaranteed to enforce grid.read.

severity.rationale: Remote authenticated low-privilege users can bypass the central graph-read permission and read TAP-managed object data. The route is designed for HTMX fragments but is directly reachable and accepts request-selected ViewerPanel targets.

findings.summary: The generic /panel/<slug>--<uuid>/ route resolves a Panel and renders its template without a grid.read authorization decision. A capless authenticated user received 200 over the Docker-published HTTP port, and a ViewerPanel instance could be pointed at another entity by query string to reveal fields that /object/... correctly denied.
findings.title: Generic panel endpoint lets no-cap users read panel content and request-selected entity fields

validation.result: Capless local-password session over host-published Docker port received 200 for /panel/... and 200 for a ViewerPanel with entity_id/entity_type query parameters, while /object/page/... returned 403.

steps: Attacker logs in as a capless user.
Attacker requests /__nav-index.json or a known page slug.
Response reveals page URLs, names, descriptions, layout slots, and panel URL ids.
Attacker uses disclosed panel URL ids to call /panel/... and read panel content via the companion finding.

codeEvidence.explanation: The route resolves and renders the page before any graph-read authorization decision.
codeEvidence.label: Page routes render without grid.read

codeEvidence.explanation: The nav endpoint exposes page metadata from direct ORM rows without grid.read.
codeEvidence.label: Nav index enumerates pages directly

codeEvidence.explanation: The page render prepares panel URL identifiers later used by HTMX, which are also sufficient to call the unguarded panel endpoint directly.
codeEvidence.label: Page rendering exposes panel URL identifiers

confidence.rationale: Source trace shows direct ORM reads, and live HTTP validation showed capless page/nav requests returning 200 while protected graph-read routes returned 403.

preventiveControls: Static authz coverage rule for Page/Panel/Edge ORM reads in web views.
Central page-resolution service that requires CallerContext.
findings.remediation: Require grid.read at the start of landing_view, page_view, parameterized_page_view, _render_grid_placeholder fallback, and nav_index_view before Page/Edge/Panel rows are loaded. Preserve anonymous login redirects, but authenticated no-cap users should receive 403 and log an authz denial.
remediationTests: No-cap live HTTP GET for page, parameterized page, landing page, and /__nav-index.json returns 403 and emits [e5d9]/[a6b7].
tap_viewer still receives 200 for page/nav read routes.

rootCause.summary: Page/navigation rendering predates the authz backstop and uses graph ORM reads as a presentation convenience without treating the routes as graph-read entrypoints.

severity.rationale: The issue exposes graph-backed page names, descriptions, layouts, slot ids, and panel URL ids to authenticated users that lack grid.read. It is also an exploit enabler for direct panel reads.

findings.summary: The page, parameterized page, landing redirect, and nav-index routes read Page, Edge, and Panel rows directly without a grid.read authorization decision. A capless authenticated user received page content and the nav catalog, including page metadata and panel URL identifiers that chain into the panel-fragment bypass.
findings.title: Dynamic page and nav-index routes enumerate page metadata and panel URLs without grid.read

validation.result: Capless local-password session over host-published Docker port received 200 for page and nav-index routes; anonymous users were redirected to login and guarded graph APIs returned 403.

steps: Attacker logs in as a capless user.
Response enumerates registered entity types and plugin names despite missing grid.read.

codeEvidence.explanation: The route is mounted with session authentication, but it does not authorize grid.read before returning graph type metadata.
codeEvidence.label: Entity type API returns catalog without authorization

confidence.rationale: The router body is a direct EntityType.objects.all() call and live network validation returned 200 for capless users.

preventiveControls: Require every core API read router to declare the capability it enforces.
Extend authz coverage tests to include metadata/catalog endpoints.
findings.remediation: Authorize grid.read in list_entity_types before querying EntityType, or route the catalog through a gated read service. Add no-cap tests for /api/v1/entity-types/ mirroring the existing /api/v1/entities/ denial tests.
remediationTests: No-cap live HTTP GET /api/v1/entity-types/ returns 403 and emits [e5d9].

rootCause.summary: Read-only type metadata was treated as harmless API catalog data and missed the auth spec requirement that every graph read, including API read endpoints, requires grid.read.

severity.rationale: The endpoint exposes model/plugin catalog metadata rather than object contents, but the auth spec states all graph reads require grid.read and this metadata helps enumerate the instance shape.

findings.summary: The /api/v1/entity-types/ endpoint is session-authenticated but returns EntityType rows directly without checking grid.read. Live HTTP validation showed capless users receive 200 from this catalog while /api/v1/entities/ correctly returns 403.
findings.title: Entity type catalog API ignores grid.read for authenticated no-cap users

validation.result: Capless local-password session received 200 for /api/v1/entity-types/ and 403 for /api/v1/entities/.
